severity.description: The severity read vocabulary. A writer may only mint blocking|major|minor|note (READABLE_SEVERITIES is the schema's enum because a reader must be able to read records written before `nit` was retired); a blocking or major finding must name its basis in `acceptanceId` or `falsifies`.

disposition.description: Set by a disposition command (`findings defer|accept|rout`) or by the closure rule marking a finding fixed. Absent means open — a record that carries no disposition has not been decided, which is different from one disposed of as nothing.

impact.description: What else the repair will touch, as the pass that filed the finding observed. Required by the brief; forbidden by this schema until it was measured, which is why 22 of this change's own findings are invalid.

classInstances.description: Where else the same defect exists, so one revision can fix the class rather than one instance. The termination condition reads this field through a finding's transport, so a transport that drops it makes the field invisible — see track() in finding-disposition.ts.

falsifier.description: The check that must redden under this defect, so the repair is checkable rather than believed. Required by the brief on every finding.

falsifies.description: What this finding falsifies, in words, for a merge-blocking severity where no acceptance criterion covers the problem. `blocking` and `major` must carry an `acceptanceId` that the acceptance matrix holds, or this; the review record refuses one that carries neither.

insideDeclaredBoundary.description: Whether this finding lies inside the boundary the claim it is about declared. A finding past the declaration is still recorded — the declaration says where the claim stops, not that nothing exists beyond it — and the two answers are kept apart so the difference is auditable rather than hidden in a severity choice. Absent when the claim declared no boundary.
